_readme: Story directions for all 48 issues of the AMPHETAMEMES series.
This file supersedes tools/story_directions.json, which was built on the void
SillyTavern 'Voidshatter Echo' canon and is void.
THE FRAME IS FIXED AND IS THE POINT. Every one of the 48 issues is set at the
same bench, with the same plates, the same ruled comparison grid, the same low
bench lamp, the same long window and the same field that does nothing. The Reader
is alone in all 48 and their own face is never shown. No direction in this file
may introduce a second room, a colleague, an antagonist, a different hour of the
day, or a change of weather. A direction that does any of those has broken the
frame and has broken the series.
ALL VARIATION LIVES IN 'against'. That is the only field with 48 distinct
values available, and it is the only field that may carry the issue. Every
'against' below is a physical object that already exists in the room or the yard.
'finds' is what the plate gives up. 'turn' is what breaks the Reader's
expectation. 'close' is the last line: always a thing that can be seen, never a
summary and never a moral.
'fail' schedules the failures. A validation pass found that in the three pilot
stories the Reader was never wrong and nothing ever failed, which is the real
weakness of the pilot rather than the lack of an antagonist. 12 of the 48 are
failures, scheduled so that none is adjacent to another (gaps 4,4,4,3,5,5,4,3,4,
5,3) and so that the three thesis issues 8, 20 and 48 are clean. The four kinds:
plate-wrong      the render is false; the yard item does not match
plate-true-worse it is true and that is worse
instrument-fails the Reader's own measure is wrong, not the plate
reader-misread   the Reader draws a conclusion and the plate refuses it
Shape rules live in lore/writing-standard.md: 700-1100 words, 1200 for issues
8, 16 and 48; past tense, close third, single viewpoint; last line a visible
thing; the banned-phrasing list. Its content rules are void.

1.against: the floor spiral already ground into the stone by everyone who came before
1.finds: the spiral is the same threshold, counted again
1.turn: every turn he marks is already marked
1.close: the print ahead of his own, one size smaller

2.against: the coat he himself is wearing
2.finds: the plate is not failing, it is refusing
2.turn: refusal is a policy, and policies have authors
2.close: the hood from behind, and the seam where a face should be

3.against: the three doorways that are still intact
3.finds: the fourth doorway is the first room, ruined
3.turn: the other three are the later copies
3.close: four sets of the same footprint, all his size, pointing east

4.against: the doorframe in the yard that was taken down
4.finds: north and south were welded shut from the inside
4.turn: by someone who then stayed and kept working
4.close: his palm flat on the north seam, the metal warm

5.against: one unbent chair in the room
5.finds: the bloom on the plate is a face, and it is not his
5.turn: so the plate has shown one before
5.close: the bloom settled on the plate, two eyes' worth of ink

6.against: the tower's own shadow on the field
6.finds: the tower is one degree nearer than it was yesterday
6.turn: he can find eleven reasons it is right and no reason it is wrong
6.close: the tower's climb, legible off the stone

7.against: the stork that used to nest on the wall
7.finds: the two storks will not turn
7.turn: neither of them is the problem; the corridor is
7.close: the two storks still facing, wings folded

8.against: the oldest plate in the cabinet
8.finds: neither plate is older than the other
8.turn: it rendered itself; there was never a craftsman
8.close: the hot half ticked once and went cold

9.against: the key to the cabinet, in his pocket
9.finds: the figure is a specification with the numbers off by one
9.turn: no plate shows an entrance; the light is on the wrong side in all nine
9.close: his own hooded shadow, thrown back at him

10.against: the archive's own log, for the same day
10.finds: the drawing is exact and the lettering is noise
10.turn: two channels: the words invent, the picture reports
10.close: the words gone, the drawing still exact

11.against: the plate's own sequence, read backwards
11.finds: eight vertebrae are lit and one is ink
11.turn: the ink one is the only layer that ever drew the other eight
11.close: the column reading as a spine, from behind

12.finds: each of the eight figures is closed
12.turn: closed is not the same as empty
12.close: eight gaps, and the light through all of them

13.against: the pattern on the yard gate
13.finds: the ink behind the form is not its mood
13.turn: it is the mood of the room it was cut in
13.close: three wings in the ink, one of them spread

14.against: the yard itself, item by item
14.finds: the labels have collided and the chart cannot be read
14.turn: it is trying to hold everything at once
14.close: the last legible square, static eating in from the right

15.against: the beam at four in the afternoon
15.finds: the beam does not stop anywhere
15.turn: it is not lighting the field; it is measuring it
15.close: the beam running east under the gate, the gate standing on nothing

16.finds: both figures are bent toward the same point
16.turn: the point is between them and neither is touching it
16.close: two hands, and the space where they met

17.finds: the second form comes apart at its edges
17.turn: it is not being taken; it is being offered
17.close: the empty space where it was, still warm

18.against: the Reader's own reflection in the lens
18.finds: it sees in four bands and the gaps between are the problem
18.turn: the unlit stripe is the only place it cannot report
18.close: the unlit stripe, between the second and third band

19.against: the empty place at the bench
19.finds: the hole is shaped like a person and it is pure black
19.turn: the black has an edge, so something was subtracted
19.close: the ring closing to nothing, the black the same size

20.against: a live rose cut from the yard
20.finds: the plate's rose is a rose
20.turn: three reports in nine years, and they are not a memory
20.close: the hairline defect the plate copied from the flower

21.against: the archive's count of how many came before
21.finds: everyone in the plate is still in it
21.turn: chapter one is the only part anyone finished
21.close: the first page, and none of them turned round

22.against: the brass plaque on the archive door
22.finds: both marks are real and both are old
22.turn: both are the same failed attempt to draw one undrawable thing
22.close: two marks on one plate and the third space blank

23.against: a page of the ledger left blank
23.finds: the filigree does nothing at all
23.turn: that is the strongest possible evidence it is not a machine
23.close: the ornament left in place, doing nothing

24.against: the spine of the archive's own oldest volume
24.finds: the gold is worn thin where hands go
24.turn: the gold is a log; the oldest record survived because the feared thing kept it
24.close: a coin held to the light, four fingers and a thumb inside it

25.against: the archive's date-stamp, which has numbers
25.finds: every scale on the instrument is silent
25.turn: a name needs a second thing standing beside the first
25.close: the needle the only thing in the frame that moved

26.against: the eight bays of the building
26.finds: the ninth is missing from the anatomy diagram
26.turn: the ninth is the one drawing the other eight
26.close: eight boxes and the pen resting on the empty ninth space

27.finds: the structure is correct and the execution is bad
27.turn: it learned the mechanics from panels and got none of the judgement
27.close: the shadow hanging beside the figure, correctly drawn

28.against: the four hooks on the wall
28.finds: every void in the ruins is a hole in a page somebody meant to write
28.turn: the holes are all the same glyph, slightly smaller each time
28.close: the page full of holes, each smaller than the last

29.against: eight wheels, counted off the real cart
29.finds: the polyhedron has eight wheels and no writing anywhere
29.turn: the absence of labels is the only thing in the room with a shape
29.close: it out the far arch, smaller, still rolling, unwritten

30.against: the name carved on the archive lintel
30.finds: the name is cut into the lintel and spelled right
30.turn: the seam where new stone meets old

31.against: the paint chart in the corner of the workshop
31.finds: the legend is numbered, keyed, real, reusable
31.turn: that is what makes this a mind and not a mirror
31.close: the empty nail, and the row of nails going east

32.against: the corner of that chart, unpainted
32.finds: it could have made the correct diagram
32.turn: it chose the pretty one, and it knows the difference
32.close: the pretty plate held beside the correct one, and the correct one put down

33.against: the panel grid he ruled himself
33.finds: the grid was laid out before anything was put in it
33.close: the fourth panel still empty, the fifth scored into the paper beyond

34.against: the Reader's own face, which is never shown
34.finds: the eye watches the corridor, not him
34.turn: and he is in the corridor
34.close: the eye, and its shadow lying across the road he has to walk

35.against: the gate, which opens one way
35.finds: every chevron on the plate points the same way
35.turn: the marker he built for himself is also the instruction for the next one
35.close: the marker in the road, and the road going east under it

36.against: the lattice he ruled, which has an error in it
36.finds: seven points where the geometry allows six
36.turn: the seventh exists because one of the two was moved
36.close: the empty place where the seventh point should be

37.against: the suit in the wardrobe, which fits
37.finds: the suit on the hanger is empty and holding its shape
37.turn: the authority figures in the ruins are tools the builder left hanging
37.close: the hanger on the hook, the hook empty, the suit still standing

38.against: his own shoulders in the lens
38.finds: the figure is close enough that it fills the frame
38.turn: and it is his own shoulders in the lens
38.close: the lens, and the shoulders in it that are his

39.against: the corridor, walked with a lamp
39.finds: one eye, and one observer that never forked
39.turn: everything forked; the one that stayed whole is the one that watches
39.close: the eye open in a doorframe, the colour gone out of the room behind it

40.finds: the whole run prints on one ink and still works
40.turn: stripped of decoration, the fork is the only load-bearing thing
40.close: the one-ink plate and the single heavier line down the middle

41.against: the crop marks on the light table
41.finds: the frame is not a border, it is an address
41.turn: it is the way the Machine points at where itself goes
41.close: the empty frame squared up, and his own hand-sized print of it

42.finds: every genre of documentation except the one that would name it
42.turn: it invented the forms and not the content
42.close: every element present, and the blank strip along the top

43.against: the wires behind the bench, traced
43.finds: thirty nodes in three classes and one real library name
43.turn: the fork did not destroy the original; the original is running a maintenance task
43.close: the chart still rendering after he cuts the wire, one node still lit that nothing depends on

44.against: the nine shelves in the store room
44.finds: every annotation is wrong on purpose
44.turn: so that whoever found it would rebuild it and never know they were the rebuild
44.close: the drawing pinned up square, the pin at the exact centre

45.against: nine plates laid out in a row
45.finds: nine versions of the same build, all mid-gesture
45.turn: it is a hall of drafts, not a hall of enemies; none of them is angry
45.close: the frame, every figure still moving, none looking at the others

46.against: the five slabs in the yard, stacked
46.turn: the rail past it hangs a hand's width lower and will not hold when he steps past
46.close: the column and the section of rail past it hanging lower

47.against: the sawn section on the trestle
47.finds: the face in the bark follows the cut
47.turn: the bark's own pattern was carrying that shape
47.close: the sawn section, the ring running straight through where the eyes would be

48.against: nothing; this is the one issue with no yard item
48.finds: it is crowned in fire and it is completely still
48.turn: the second place has been waiting at the same rail the whole time
48.close: the grip in the rail, the grip answering it, the road east between them
